changes.title: Report a bug or suggest an idea from the app
changes.body: From the Help menu, ⌘K, /bug or /feedback in a message box, or the crash screen, with the last 30 minutes of the log if you want it (tokens, emails and paths taken out). Settings › Feedback shows where each report stands.

changes.title: The sidebar groups threads by who acts next
changes.body: Needs you, Ready to merge, Working and Done, with every thread under the right heading. Settings › Labs turns the headings off.

changes.title: See what's new in every version
changes.body: In Settings › What's new and on tryensemble.co/changelog; the update popup lists what an update brings.

changes.title: Git & GitHub settings
changes.body: A page of its own in Settings, with how much of GitHub's hourly limit is left.

changes.title: Start a thread from another thread's work or a branch
changes.body: The new-thread form says where a thread starts, and lists threads' work and branches the default branch doesn't have yet.

changes.title: Open a pull request on GitHub with ⌘-click
changes.body: Or a middle click on its button in the status bar (Ctrl-click on Linux and Windows). A pull request GitHub refuses says which field was wrong.

changes.title: New thread opens as a page of its own
changes.body: ⌘N, a project's + and ⌘K show it in the window instead of a dialog, with the project's to-dos to start from. With no thread open, the window shows it too.

changes.title: A cleaner light theme
changes.body: Cool greys, a white message box and soft shadows, where the dark theme's shadows used to turn into grey smudges.

changes.title: An agent can fix a service that fails to start
changes.body: When a service in the Running tab exits with an error, send its output to the agent: it fixes the cause, adds what was missing to the project's setup and starts the service again.

changes.title: A thread archives itself once its pull request merges
changes.body: Keep it instead with Settings › Labs › Keep a thread after its PR merges. The chat says Merged once, not twice.

changes.title: Agents ask only when they need you
changes.body: They no longer stop to ask whether to open a pull request, and when they do need you to choose, the thread shows it's waiting on you.

changes.title: A quieter message box
changes.body: The agent's suggested next steps above it are gone; what it shows you stays in its reply.

changes.title: Faster starts after an update
changes.body: The app keeps what it read from your machines across updates, and shows one sync screen while they catch up instead of the sidebar flickering through old states.

changes.title: A smaller thread card on hover
changes.body: Title, branch, what it's about, its changes, agent, machine and time, shown as soon as you point at a thread, and switching at once as you move to the next one.

changes.title: Unread threads stay unread after a restart
changes.body: And threads that finished while the app was closed come back marked.

changes.title: Cleaner diagrams, and a lighter app
changes.body: Diagrams in replies are drawn with straight lines in the app's own colours, in both themes, and every kind fits its frame. The app itself got smaller.

changes.title: Git's buttons have icons
changes.body: Create PR, Push, Merge, Continue, Reopen and Archive carry an icon, and the quiet ones take the status bar's colour.

changes.title: Ensemble's own icon in Login Items
changes.body: On a Mac, the helper that keeps your threads running in the background shows the app's icon in System Settings.

changes.title: macOS no longer autocorrects what you type to the agent
changes.body: It swapped words as you typed, like "pr" for "project". Its inline suggestions stay.

changes.title: Betas too works on Linux and Windows
changes.body: Betas were made for Macs only, so the app elsewhere couldn't check for updates on that channel. Every beta now comes for all three.

changes.title: Pull requests stay current without using up GitHub's hourly limit
changes.body: The app asks GitHub only about what changed, and keeps some of the limit for what you do yourself.

changes.title: New threads start from the latest default branch
changes.body: A folder project that was behind GitHub started threads from an old copy of it.

changes.title: This Mac's machine starts every time
changes.body: On some Macs its background helper was loaded but never started, and the app only said "connection closed".

changes.title: Claude no longer forgets a conversation by mistake
changes.body: A reply that only quoted Claude's "No conversation found" message made the next turn start afresh.

changes.title: A thread moved to an Ensemble VM always keeps its work
changes.body: If a move can't bring the work along, it stops and says why.

changes.title: The context meter is right from a chat's first turn
changes.body: On newer Claude models a new chat no longer looks fuller than it is before its first reply ends.

changes.title: The sidebar keeps its order and its folds
changes.body: Projects without threads stay listed, and a folded section stays folded with one of its threads open.

changes.title: Long paths and lists wrap in a sent message
changes.body: Instead of running off the chat's left edge.

changes.title: Choose repositories opens GitHub again
Get new versions early
changes.body: Settings › General › Updates: choose Betas too to get each new version before everyone else.

changes.title: The app opens again after updating
changes.body: Some conversations made 0.2.8's window break as soon as it opened.

changes.title: No more crashes when a thread starts or stops working
changes.body: And if the window does break, it offers the update that fixes it.

changes.title: Stacked pull requests
changes.body: A thread can build on another's branch; its pull request targets that branch and merges after it. Every step that's yours shows in the inbox and the sidebar.

changes.title: See when each usage limit resets
changes.body: The usage popover shows each agent's limits, when they reset, and whether you're on pace.

changes.title: Choose which logins to use, and when to switch
changes.body: In Settings › Agents, turn each login on or off, drag them into the order you want, and set how much of a limit to use before moving on.

changes.title: Ask an agent to archive a thread
Updates never cut a running turn off
changes.body: Your machines update quietly in the background, and agents carry on where they were.

changes.title: Start a thread the moment you add a project
Ensemble VMs try again when a start fails
changes.body: Folders with a GitHub remote work there too.

changes.title: A Claude token pasted from a terminal just works
Agents answer with pages of data
changes.body: Numbers, charts, tables, timelines and flows, drawn right in the reply in the app's own style.

changes.title: Agents can point you to another thread
changes.body: It shows as a chip you can click to open it.

changes.title: Ensemble VMs run folder projects
Code blocks with highlighting and a copy button
Projects that use Git LFS start threads
Ensemble for Windows
changes.body: Download the installer from the website; threads run in Git for Windows' shell.

changes.title: Merge conflicts go to the agent
changes.body: Press Merge on a pull request that conflicts and the agent merges the base in for you to look over, instead of the merge failing.

changes.title: Check for updates from Settings
A quieter top bar
changes.body: It shows the machine's icon and short name.

changes.title: The sidebar marks threads with a message you haven't sent
changes.body: And gives each title more room.

changes.title: The status bar no longer flickers, or says merged before it is
Dictate your messages
changes.body: Speak into the message box on a Mac, with Apple's speech recognition.

changes.title: Attach any file to a message
changes.body: Up to 5 MB each.

changes.title: Move a thread to a bigger VM
changes.body: From the move menu, or ask the agent when a build needs more room.

changes.title: The chat says when its pull request is merged, closed or reopened
Get started suggests your projects
changes.body: The repositories Claude Code and Codex have worked in are offered as projects.

changes.title: Take over a thread an agent started
changes.body: Threads an agent starts report to it and are read-only to you, until you take one over.

changes.title: Threads sorted by what they need from you
Checks that need you come first
changes.body: Passed ones are folded away.

changes.title: A dropped file goes where your cursor is in the message
See when an update is ready
changes.body: Above the sidebar's foot, with a restart button.

changes.title: Archiving a thread with an open pull request asks first
Ensemble's first release
changes.body: Run Claude Code and Codex threads side by side, each in a machine of its own, on your Mac or your own servers.
